title: Eight Cron Jobs Became One 30-Second Loop | vitalii.no
description:
Why a memecoin trading bot with eight separate jobs kept fighting itself, and how a single scheduled loop replaced eight competing timers.

Building a trading bot that scans for new coins, pulls market data, scores risk, decides whether to buy, executes trades, launches new tokens, collects fees and guards a treasury limit normally means a choice between one bloated program or eight separate scheduled jobs. The second option sounds cleaner, but all eight end up reaching for the same rows in the same database at the same moment, stepping on each other's state.

The fix was a single Durable Object called Desk that owns one alarm loop firing every 30 seconds. Each cycle walks through all eight agents in a fixed order — scanning, enriching, scoring, deciding, trading, launching, collecting, and guarding — all reading and writing one shared database, so there is one consistent view of the market instead of eight processes racing each other. A once-a-minute scheduled trigger only watches the loop and restarts it if it ever stalls.

The whole desk now runs inside one Worker and one Durable Object, no server to maintain, coordinated by a single loop instead of eight competing schedules.
